questions.question:

questions.solution:
The correct answer is: **Option 3** i.e. **Attack**.

• The word **"Secure"** means to make safe, protect, or guard something against danger or harm. (सुरक्षित करना)

• **"Attack"** refers to an aggressive action against someone or something, typically with the intent to harm or damage. (हमला करना)
 
 
• **Example:** The soldiers were prepared to attack the enemy at dawn.
 
 
 
• Hence, we can infer that the opposite of **'Secure'** is **'Attack'**.

• **Example:** The old cart trundled down the bumpy road.

questions.question:
Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence.

Gourav was __no good__ than a foolish person.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 1**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The primary issue in the sentence is the use of the word "**good**" in the comparison.
 
• In comparative sentences, "**better**" is the correct form to use.
 
• The correct phrase should be "**no better**," ensuring grammatical correctness and clarity.

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 1**.

 

**Correct Sentence:** *"Gourav was no better than a foolish person."*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 2: "not good"** – This phrase is not correct as it does not provide a proper comparative structure.
 
• **Option 3: "no best"** – This phrase is incorrect as "best" is the superlative form and does not fit in this context.
 
• **Option 4: "not best"** – This phrase is also incorrect because it lacks proper comparative structure and "best" should be used in superlative form.

questions.question:

He ran quick to catch the bus.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 4**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The primary issue in the sentence is the use of the adjective "quick" instead of the adverb "quickly."
 
• Adverbs modify verbs and usually end in "-ly."
 
• The correct phrase should be "He ran quickly to catch the bus," ensuring grammatical correctness and clarity.

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 4**.

 

**Correct Sentence:** *"He ran quickly to catch the bus."*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Quick** is an adjective that modifies nouns.
 
• **Quickly** is an adverb that modifies verbs, adjectives, or other adverbs.
 
• Using the correct form of the word ensures that the sentence is grammatically correct.

questions.question:
Select the option that expresses the following sentence in passive voice.

Sonam does not like bananas.

options.text: Banana is not liked by Sonam.
Bananas have not been liked by Sonam.
Bananas are not liked by Sonam.
Bananas had not been liked by Sonam.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 3**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Passive voice structure: The object of the active voice sentence becomes the subject of the passive voice sentence.
 
• In the active voice, the sentence is: "Sonam does not like bananas."
 
• To convert to passive voice: Place the object "bananas" at the beginning.
 
• Change the active verb form "does not like" to "are not liked" (present simple passive).
 
• Ensure the subject "Sonam" remains, but the focus is on the object "bananas."

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 3**.

 

**Correct Sentence:** *"Bananas are not liked by Sonam."*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 1: **"Banana is not liked by Sonam." – Incorrect, as "banana" is singular instead of the plural "bananas."
 
• **Option 2: **"Bananas have not been liked by Sonam." – Incorrect tense (present perfect passive).
 
• **Option 4: **"Bananas had not been liked by Sonam." – Incorrect tense (past perfect passive).

questions.question:
Sentences of a paragraph are given below in jumbled order. Arrange the sentences in the correct order to form a meaningful and coherent paragraph.

A. The genuine beliefs, though not unconsciously acquired by most children; and even if they depart from these beliefs in later life

B. Something of them remains deeply implanted, ready to emerge in a time of stress of crisis

C. The importance of education in forming character and opinion is very great and well recognised by all

D. Education is, as a rule, the strongest force on the side of what exists and again fundamental change
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option (3)** i.e. **CABD**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The paragraph begins with the sentence “The importance of education in forming character and opinion is very great and well recognised by all,” which sets the topic of the paragraph. This is indicated by **part C**.
 
• Next, **part A**, this sentence connects to C by elaborating on the influence of education in forming beliefs in children. It builds on the idea of how education shapes these beliefs, even if the beliefs may not last forever.
 
• **Part B** following A, this sentence explains how even if beliefs formed during education are altered over time, a part of them remains ingrained, ready to resurface during challenging situations.
 
• **Finally, part D** concludes by discussing the significant role education plays in maintaining existing beliefs, which supports the overall argument of the paragraph.

Therefore, the correct answer is **CABD.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 1 (DCAB):** This option starts with “Education is, as a rule, the strongest force,” which disrupts the logical flow of the paragraph.
 
• **Option 2 (DABC):** This option also begins with part D, which does not smoothly lead into the other sentences.
 
• **Option 3 (CBAD):** This option disrupts the sequence by discussing lasting beliefs (B) before their formation (A).

questions.question:
Select the option that expresses the given sentence in passive voice

Someone has taken my secret diary.

options.text: My secret diary had been taken by someone.
My secret diary has to be taken by someone.
My secret diary has been taken by someone.
My secret diary will have been taken by someone.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 3**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In passive voice, the object of the active sentence becomes the subject of the passive sentence.
 
• In the active voice, the sentence is: "Someone has taken my secret diary."
 
• To convert it to passive: the object "my secret diary" is placed at the beginning.
 
• The verb "has taken" is converted to "has been taken" (present perfect passive).
 
• The subject "someone" remains optional, but the sentence still makes sense without it.

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 3**.

 

**Correct Sentence:** *"My secret diary has been taken by someone."*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 1: **"My secret diary had been taken by someone." – Incorrect tense (past perfect passive).
 
• **Option 2: **"My secret diary has to be taken by someone." – Incorrect structure and meaning (necessity is implied, which is not the original intent).
 
• **Option 4: **"My secret diary will have been taken by someone." – Incorrect tense (future perfect passive).

questions.question:
Select the most appropriate synonym of the bracketed word in the following sentence to fill in the blank.

During Covid times, many organisations made _______ (sentimental) appeals to raise funds for migrant workers.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is: **Option 1**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The word **"sentimental"** refers to feelings of nostalgia, tenderness, or excessive emotion often tied to memories. (भावुक)

 
 
• **Example:** His sentimental attachment to his childhood home made it hard for him to sell it.
 
 
 
• **"Mawkish"** means excessively sentimental in a way that is insincere or overly emotional, often to the point of being cloying or unpleasant. (अत्यधिक भावुक या नकल करने वाला)
 
 
• **Example:** The mawkish love story in the movie made some viewers uncomfortable due to its melodrama.
 
 

Therefore, the correct answer is: **Option 1**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

Here are the other options explained along with their Hindi meanings and example sentences:

 
• **Option 2: "Sincere"** (ईमानदार): This refers to being genuine and free from pretense, which is not the same as being overly emotional or sentimental.

 
 
• **Example:** Her sincere apology was well received by everyone in the room.
 
 
 
• **Option 3: "Cynical"** (निंदक): This refers to a belief that people are primarily motivated by self-interest and is not related to sentimentality.
 
 
• **Example:** His cynical view of politics led him to believe that no one was genuinely interested in making a difference.
 
 
 
• **Option 4: "Practical"** (व्यावहारिक): Refers to something based on real-world applications or logic, which contrasts with emotional or sentimental appeals.
 
 
• **Example:** His practical approach to problem-solving helped streamline the project and deliver results on time.

questions.question:
Select the option that will improve the underlined part of the given sentence.

If I __was the queen__, I would give a handsome sum towards education.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 2**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The sentence involves a hypothetical situation, which is expressed using the second conditional. This form requires "were" instead of "was" after "if" for correct usage in formal English.
 
• In second conditional sentences, we use "if + subject + were" to describe unreal situations or hypothetical scenarios.
 
• Thus, the correct form in the sentence is "**were the queen**".

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 2**.

 

**Correct Sentence:** *"If I were the queen, I would give a handsome sum towards education."*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 1: "If I will be the queen"** – Incorrect, as the future tense ("will") is not used in second conditional sentences.
 
• **Option 3: "If I have been the queen"** – Incorrect, as this form is in the present perfect tense, which does not fit the context of a hypothetical scenario.
 
• **Option 4: "If I would be the queen"** – Incorrect, as "would" is used in the result clause of conditional sentences, not in the "if" clause.
